approach: Add one settle step at job close. In `close_dispatched` (and the gate-refused Failed branch of `land_or_block`), when the outcome is rejected, failed or timed_out and the job has an early PR link, the closing commit gets a new small record `athena.pull-request/1` at `<job dir>/pull-request.json` holding the job id, PR number and repository. After that commit succeeds, `settle_pr` calls two new `PrHost` methods. A rejected job, or a failed job that is not resumable, gets `close_pr`: `POST issues/{n}/comments` then `PATCH pulls/{n}` with `state=closed`. A job a retry resumes from (timed_out, or failed for an environment reason) gets `comment_pr` only, a not-landing mark, and stays open. Landed, stale, blocked and every other state, and any job with no link, make no host call. A host error becomes one warning line and never changes the recorded outcome. The decision and calls live in `gh/early.rs` beside `open_early_pr`. The test seam is the existing `early_seam` plus `EarlyFake`, extended with recorded PR calls. A design section, a records.md row and a changelog line are added.

decisions.choice: Record the PR number in a new job-level record `athena.pull-request/1` (`<job dir>/pull-request.json`: job, pr_number, repository), written in the closing commit before any host call.
decisions.reason: `Outcome` has `deny_unknown_fields` and about 16 files build `Outcome` literals (status.rs, steward.rs, manage.rs, gate tests, cli tests and others), so a new field would touch all of them. A new `AnyRecord` variant touches `canonical_path`, `schema` and `parse` in athena-data, plus the one `job_of` arm in store.rs. `job_of` ends in `.expect("every other record names its job")` for any record not matched earlier, so a job-level variant without an arm would panic when records load. The record is written first, so a crash between the commit and the host call leaves the number recorded. It holds only the job id, number and repository, so nothing needs redacting.

rejected.why: It touches every `Outcome` literal across seven crates and tests, which is not one focused change.

rejected.option: Put the number in the outcome `reason` text.
rejected.why: It is free text, not queryable, and would change reason strings that tests and the score read.

rejected.option: Keep the number only in the state-dir `pr-link.json`.
rejected.why: That is the status quo: the file is outside the repository, so "no job record names its PR" would stay true.

decisions.choice: Decide per outcome: rejected -> close; failed -> close unless `crate::disk::is_environment_reason(reason)`, then keep open; timed_out -> keep open; landed, stale, blocked and all other states -> untouched.
decisions.reason: `athena retry` resumes only a timed_out job or a failed job with an environment reason (`resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` in run/mod.rs:860-874). Those are the jobs whose PR 'must stay open for a retry'. The other non-landing outcomes are final. Verified jobs (landed, stale, blocked) are never touched, as the brief requires.

rejected.option: Close every non-landing PR, retries included.
rejected.why: It contradicts the request's retry clause. It would also close the PR of a job whose kept candidate is about to be resumed.
Failed jobs are named in the request, and the root cause is the missing close at job close for every non-landing outcome.

decisions.choice: Add two required `PrHost` methods, `comment_pr(number, body)` and `close_pr(number, comment)`. `GhClient::close_pr` is `comment_pr` then `PATCH repos/{r}/pulls/{n}` with `-f state=closed`, both through `GhClient::api`, recorded under `HostOperation::CreatePr`.
decisions.reason: This follows the existing REST-only, retrying wrapper, so the guard in `crates/athena-core/tests/external_calls_guard.rs` stays satisfied. `HostOperation` is a closed list (rerun reused `ReadChecks` for this reason). `CreatePr` is the pull-request write operation, and the watcher only fires on Merge, so no signal changes. The comment goes first as the brief says. Its text says Athena is closing the PR, so a failed PATCH leaves a truthful comment.

rejected.why: It widens a persisted enum (`ALL`, `parse`, `as_str`) and the host-error records for one call.
The brief orders comment then close. A closed PR with no comment loses the reason if the second call fails.

rejected.option: A mark by editing the title or adding a label.
rejected.why: A title edit needs a read-modify-write and a label needs another REST call and permission. A comment is one call and visible on the PR.

decisions.choice: Put the decision, comment text and `settle_pr(host, link, state, reason)` in `gh/early.rs`, plus an `Athena::settle_pr` wrapper (seam or `GhCli`/`GhClient`) in the same style as `early_pr`. Wire it from `close_dispatched` and from the gate-refused Failed branch of `land_or_block`.
decisions.reason: A job's PR is opened in this file, so the close belongs beside it. The pure function is testable with `FakeHost` in `gh/tests.rs`, and the wrapper through `Athena::go` with `EarlyFake`. Hooking the close step rather than one outcome fixes the root cause for every non-landing outcome. The comment holds only the job id and outcome word (public rule).

rejected.why: The closing commit is already built by then, so the number could not go into it.
The closed `gh/mod.rs` module list would grow for about 80 lines. `early.rs` is the PR lifecycle file.

decisions.choice: Leave `PrLink`/`LinkState` unchanged. Do not touch the landing path (`land_pr`, `gh/landing.rs`, `gh/records.rs`). Do not add a Closed link state.
decisions.reason: The brief forbids changing landing or merge behavior for verified jobs. No landing code needs the new state, since a closed PR belongs to a job that never lands. The two deliverable files `landing.rs` and `records.rs` are therefore not edited; the expected list is a ceiling, not a requirement.

rejected.why: It would change serde and match arms in landing for no reader.

risks.risk: A host error on the comment or close could change a job's outcome or abort `go`.
risks.mitigation: `settle_pr` returns a Result and the `Athena::settle_pr` wrapper turns any error into one `warning: could not close the pull request #N: ...` line, after the closing commit is made. A test with `fail_close` checks the outcome is unchanged and the record is present.

risks.risk: The comment is posted but the PATCH then fails, leaving an open PR with a 'closing' comment.
risks.mitigation: The comment says Athena is closing the PR and names the job and outcome. The error path prints a warning that tells the user the PR is still open. Comment-then-PATCH is the order the brief asks for.

risks.risk: A PR kept open for a retry is never closed afterwards.
risks.mitigation: A retry runs as a new job with its own PR, so the old PR stays open with a not-landing comment. The gap is stated in the design section and raised as an open question. The old PR is at least clearly marked.

risks.risk: The landing or verified path changes by accident.
risks.mitigation: The disposition list is explicit (rejected, failed, timed_out), and a test covers landed, stale and blocked. The record is only pushed in the non-landing path. The Landed branch of `close_dispatched` and all landing code have no diff.

risks.risk: The new record kind breaks a reader (`job_of` panic or a gate rule).
risks.mitigation: Adding the `PullRequest` variant forces the compiler to flag every exhaustive match. The dependents list shows each match checked and the one `expect` fixed in store.rs. A run test loads records after a rejected GitHub job.

risks.risk: `gh api` retries a POST on a transient error and could post a duplicate comment.
risks.mitigation: The retry wrapper is the existing one. The window is small and the effect is a repeated comment, not a wrong state. The PATCH is idempotent.

risks.risk: The extra ui line breaks an existing test that scans lines.
risks.mitigation: The success line is `pr         #7 closed` or `pr         #7 marked not landing`, with no `warning` text. The full `cargo test` is run to confirm.

demonstrations.method: `records::tests::a_job_pull_request_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips` builds the record, checks `schema()` is `athena.pull-request/1`, round-trips `to_json` and `AnyRecord::parse`, passes `check_record_file` at `<job dir>/pull-request.json`, and gets `RecordError::Misplaced` at another path. `an_invalid_job_pull_request_is_refused` covers a zero number and an empty repository. The run test from criterion 1 reads the written file back. `git diff` shows the record written in the closing commit.
demonstrations.observes: The record is accepted at its canonical path and refused elsewhere. The closing commit of a rejected GitHub job contains it with `pr_number` 7.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `canonical_path` arm the file does not compile. With a wrong path the `Misplaced` assertion flips. Without the `job_of` arm in store.rs, `Records::load` panics in the criterion-1 run test, which loads records at HEAD.
demonstrations.seam: `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (exist, read at lines 1049-1409). The new variant is added in step 1. `Records::load` is exercised by the existing run-test helpers.

demonstrations.observes: All pass. The existing tests are textually unchanged: only additions, plus new `pr_calls` and `fail_close` fields in the `EarlyFake` constructor and new trait-method impls in the fakes. `land_or_block`'s landing arm, `land_pr`, `landing.rs` and `records.rs` have no diff, and the Landed branch of `close_dispatched` is untouched.

demonstrations.method: `run::tests::a_failed_close_is_one_warning_and_the_outcome_stays` sets `fail_close` on the `EarlyFake` (step 6), runs `ci_run(Some(GITHUB), FAILS_ON_EDIT, false, |f| f.fail_close.set(true))` and compares the state with a run without it. `run::tests::no_github_origin_means_no_pull_request_calls_and_no_record` loops over the origins used by the existing test at run/tests.rs:5535-5541 and asserts the fake's `pr_calls` is empty and no `pull-request.json` exists. A unit test, `a_refused_close_is_an_error_and_leaves_the_link_unchanged`, covers `settle_pr`.
demonstrations.observes: With a refused close: state is still `Rejected`, exactly one line starts with `warning: could not close the pull request`, and the record is still committed. With no origin, or none of the GitHub origins: zero PR calls and no record. `settle_pr` returns `Err` and the stored link equals the original.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `settle_pr` propagated the error with `?` out of `close_dispatched`, `go` would return Err and `finished(..).unwrap()` panics. Without the link guard, a no-origin job would call the host and `pr_calls` would not be empty.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go` via `ci_run` with `EarlyFake.fail_close` (added in step 6) installed through `early_seam` (exists). The fake only refuses; the decision and the warning are the production code's.

open_questions: User: When a retry (a new job that resumes a timed_out or environment-failed job) finishes, should its close also close the PR of the job it resumed from? Today that old PR keeps the not-landing comment and stays open, because a retry opens its own PR under its own job id. This plan leaves it as a documented gap.
Host: Does the token `gh` uses in the target repositories have write access to pull requests and issues (comments)? A token without it makes every close a warning line, never a changed outcome.

User: Should a verified job whose landing commit the gate refuses (the Failed branch inside `land_or_block`) have its PR closed? This plan treats it as failed, so it is closed and recorded. If you read it as a verified job, drop that one call and the records push.
